concerns.concern: The light-induced erasure may be a heating effect or an artefact of LED output changing with temperature, not an optical effect. No photon flux, spectrum, on-sample temperature, heater-pulse control, or power/wavelength dependence is reported.
concerns.quote: Optical versus thermal origin of the erasure is not established.

concerns.concern: T_c may simply follow the normal-state mobility and resistance in every protocol, which would make the PNR-mediated pairing claim unnecessary. The authors should plot T_c against μ, R_s and n for all states to test whether the points collapse onto one curve.
concerns.quote: T_c may simply track the normal-state transport, independent of PNR-mediated pairing.

concerns.concern: The claim of complete erasure is not checked against the pristine, never-gated state. The illuminated state appears to be a distinct higher-carrier-density state rather than a reset to the origin.
concerns.quote: "Complete erasure" is not demonstrated against the pristine state.

concerns.concern: Extrapolating the dielectric Arrhenius parameters to the slow transport timescales gives characteristic temperatures that do not match the 35 K and 95 K features. The nearly temperature-independent relaxation time is also inconsistent with an activated process, so the link between the loss peaks and the 2DEG effects is not quantitative.
concerns.quote: qualitative, and quantitatively inconsistent with the extracted Arrhenius parameters.

concerns.concern: The assignment of the loss peaks to polar nanoregion flipping and oxygen-vacancy ionization lacks controls. The measurement probes the bulk substrate, Maxwell–Wagner relaxation or impurity dipoles could explain the peaks, and there are no reference samples, Cole–Cole analysis, impurity characterisation, phase-error assessment or uncertainties.
concerns.quote: The assignment of the loss peaks to PNR flipping and OV ionization lacks controls.

concerns.concern: The proposed oxygen-vacancy mechanism is energetically inconsistent. A 236 meV thermal barrier cannot produce hysteresis within minutes at 1.4–10 K, so any field-assisted tunnelling must be modelled explicitly.
concerns.quote: With E_a = 236 meV, the thermal rate at 10 K is effectively zero.

concerns.concern: The linear Δ_L ∝ ε relation follows trivially from induced charge Q = CV ∝ ε. The deviation below 35 K may reflect the difference between small-signal and large-signal permittivity, and it is unclear which frequency's ε is used.
concerns.quote: Any trapping hysteresis proportional to the induced charge gives Δ_L ∝ ε without invoking OV ionization physics.

concerns.concern: PNR internal gating and remnant polarization are inferred rather than measured: there is no P–E loop or butterfly ε(V_g). The authors' Hall data also show n insensitive to sweep type, which conflicts with the proposed internal gating.
concerns.quote: The PNR "internal gating" and remnant polarization are inferred, not measured.

concerns.concern: The Hall analysis uses a single band at only ±6 T and gives n increasing at negative gate, opposite to electrostatic depletion. n and μ also come from separate runs on a strongly history-dependent system. Full R_xy(B) sweeps, a two-band fit, a capacitive comparison and a reproducibility check are needed.
concerns.quote: The Hall analysis is single-band at only ±6 T and gives an anomalous sign.

concerns.concern: All results appear to come from a single device. Further samples, a room-temperature reset of the same device, and device-to-device spread are needed.
concerns.quote: Everything appears to come from one 2.5 × 2.5 mm device.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 4 relaxation analysis is fragile. Fitted τ is comparable to the observation window, each peak rests on a single temperature point, the text's 'two minima' contradicts the figure, and the illumination dose varies with temperature.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 4 analysis is fragile.

concerns.concern: Protocol controls for the gate memory are missing. These include sweep rate and dwell times, a 0 V hold control, unipolar cycles, matched pristine protocols, and charge bookkeeping from integrated gate current.
concerns.quote: Protocol controls for the gate memory are missing.

concerns.concern: The photon-energy argument is physically incorrect: thermal activation barriers being smaller than the photon energy does not mean light can drive them. Sub-gap absorption or photocurrent spectra are needed, or the claim should be removed.
concerns.quote: Thermal activation barriers are not optical transitions

concerns.concern: Superconducting characterisation is minimal. T_c is taken at 50% R_n on broad transitions, so the shifts could reflect a changing percolative network. Onset, zero-resistance point, transition width, H_c2 or I–V data are needed.
concerns.quote: The superconducting characterisation is minimal.

concerns.concern: Non-volatility is not quantified. Retention over hours to days, the effect of temperature excursions, and the limit set by dark relaxation above 15 K should be reported given the memory framing.
concerns.quote: Non-volatility is not quantified.

concerns.concern: The measured permittivity (~1600) is well below the typical ~4000 for KTO at low temperature. Electrode area and thickness should be given and the discrepancy explained, since it affects both the ε-scaling argument and tan δ.
concerns.quote: ε saturates at ≈1600 (f > 1 Hz) in Fig. 3a, well below the ≈4000 typical for KTO at low T.

concerns.concern: Novelty relative to ref. 30 is unclear, and gate-cycling enhancement of T_c is already reported there.
concerns.quote: Clarify what is new relative to ref. 30

concerns.concern: The paper should discuss known irreversible back-gate forming effects in LAO/STO and explain why the irreversibility here occurs on the negative branch.
concerns.quote: Discuss the well-known irreversible "forming" in back-gated LAO/STO

concerns.concern: Possible transport anisotropy of KTO(111) interfaces is not considered. The isotropic van der Pauw conversion to R_s needs justification, or both vdP configurations should be reported.
concerns.quote: Justify the isotropic van der Pauw/FEM conversion to R_s, or report both vdP configurations.

concerns.concern: Error bars are missing on T_c, E_a, τ, ΔR/R₁ and Δ_L throughout.
concerns.quote: Error bars are missing on T_c, E_a, τ, ΔR/R₁ and Δ_L throughout.

concerns.concern: The relaxation formula switches between Δ_L and δε = ε − ε∞ without defining ε∞ or how it is fitted.
concerns.quote: Define ε∞ and state how it is fitted.

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether the light source is a laser or an LED, and its spectrum and power are not given.
concerns.quote: state whether the source is a laser or an LED, and give its spectrum and power.

concerns.concern: Supp. Fig. 5 is labelled 'Extended Figure 5' and uses a different normalisation (ΔR₀ vs R₁) and illumination time (1300 s vs ~1000 s) from Fig. 4; these should be harmonised.
concerns.quote: It normalises by ΔR₀, whereas Fig. 4 normalises by R₁, and the illumination times differ

concerns.concern: Supp. Note 4 appears to mislabel R_s^b as R_s^a and mixes Ω and Ω·sq⁻¹ units.
concerns.quote: "R_s^b = 856 Ω·sq⁻¹" in group 2 should presumably be R_s^a.

concerns.concern: The Methods statement about keeping the LED voltage V_L the same versus holding the current I_L constant is ambiguous.
concerns.quote: "kept the same V_L" versus constant I_L is ambiguous.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3d caption phrase 'deviates above this dependence' is unclear, and the T = 35 K dashed line on an ε axis needs explanation.
concerns.quote: "deviates above this dependence" is unclear.

concerns.concern: A sentence about dielectric loss identifying two excitations is duplicated in the Discussion.
concerns.quote: the sentence about dielectric loss identifying two excitations is duplicated.

concerns.concern: The authors should verify that ref. 45 actually contains the hybrid-functional DFT result attributed to it.
concerns.quote: Verify that ref. 45 indeed contains the hybrid-functional DFT result attributed to it.

concerns.concern: There are several typos.
concerns.quote: Typos: "memrisitive", "illlumination", "Suppelementary"
